title: Your Income Tax Return (ITR) Deadline is Near!
description: The deadline to file your Income Tax Return (ITR) for the financial year 2025-26 is typically July 31, 2026. Filing your ITR is crucial, even if you don't owe.

faq.q: What is the basic exemption limit for ITR filing?
faq.a: For most individuals below 60 years of age under the old tax regime, the basic exemption limit for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) is ₹2.5 lakh. If your gross total income before claiming deductions exceeds this amount, filing an ITR is generally mandatory.

faq.q: What happens if I miss the July 31st deadline?
faq.a: If you miss the deadline, you can still file a "belated return," usually by December 31st of the assessment year. However, you will likely have to pay a late filing fee of up to ₹5,000 and interest on any unpaid tax. You also lose the ability to carry forward certain types of losses.

faq.q: Can I file my ITR using my mobile phone?
faq.a: Yes, the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal is designed to be mobile-friendly, and some third-party apps also offer ITR filing services. While it's possible, using a computer is often recommended for a smoother experience, especially if your tax situation is complex.

faq.q: How do I know which ITR form to use?
faq.a: The e-filing portal often guides you based on your income sources. Generally, ITR-1 is for salaried individuals with income from one house property and other sources like interest. ITR-2 is for those with capital gains or income from more than one house property, and ITR-3 is for individuals with income from a business or profession.

Form 26AS is like your tax passbook, showing details of tax deducted at source (TDS), tax collected at source (TCS), and any advance tax you've paid. The Annual Information Statement (AIS) is a more comprehensive statement that includes not just tax details but also other financial transactions like interest, dividends, mutual fund transactions, and foreign remittances, helping you ensure all income is declared accurately.
